holdReason: scripts/validate-knowledge-base.js applies the citation-purity threshold PER SUGGESTION: any suggestion whose unverified ratio exceeds 0.3 forces the whole mapping to draft:true (and a single-unverified-reference suggestion is immediately quarantined). With at most 3 references per suggestion, one unverified reference is already 33 percent, so NO unverified reference can enter a published mapping at all. Empirically confirmed on 2026-09-28: across all 140 published mappings (267 reference uses) the only unverified references were the eight batch-89 rows being tested. ptsd is a published mapping carrying 19 qualified-human-verified edges; flipping it to draft:true would unpublish those edges and break the 140/673 published/draft pin, and adding the edges with verified:false references fails kb:validate four-to-one. The four edges were therefore reverted from ptsd.json and are held here until their citations are qualified-human verified. Mapping approval is not citation verification.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: A documented post-traumatic stress disorder diagnosis is associated with incident psoriasis in one large nationwide population-based cohort, and that finding DIRECTLY CONFLICTS with the best available meta-analytic estimate for the same exposure class, so the edge is registered at association only with the disagreement carried on its face and NOT resolved: the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database cohort of 9,801 patients with PTSD matched to 39,204 controls reports an adjusted hazard ratio for psoriasis of 3.81 (95 percent CI 1.90-7.67) and for autoimmune skin disease overall of 3.00 (2.21-4.07) by adjusted Cox regression (PMID 33587564); against which the 2018 systematic review and meta-analysis of 39 studies and 32,537 patients reports that the ONLY study evaluating a DOCUMENTED STRESS DISORDER DIAGNOSIS found similar rates in patients and controls at an odds ratio of 1.2 (95 percent CI 0.8-1.8), that four of six studies of events preceding EXACERBATION reported rates comparable to controls while two found more frequent or more severe preceding events, and concludes that 'no convincing evidence exists that preceding stress is strongly associated with exacerbation/onset of psoriasis' (PMID 29124739); the same review's pooled odds ratio of 3.4 (1.8-6.4) for recalled stressful events preceding ONSET rests on five studies under I-squared 87 percent heterogeneity and on RECALLED events rather than on a diagnosis, so it does not answer the exposure this catalog identity represents. The registered claim is therefore the narrowest the two anchors jointly permit: that a PTSD diagnosis precedes and is associated with incident psoriasis in one national cohort, contradicted at the meta-analytic level for the diagnosis-based exposure, with the contradiction open.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of psoriasis is established for any individual, and the located evidence does not merely fail to establish it - it DISAGREES about it. The cohort supporting this edge measures a PTSD diagnosis against incident psoriasis at an adjusted hazard ratio of 3.81 but is administrative-claims based, cannot control for smoking, alcohol, obesity, medication adherence or healthcare-seeking intensity, and cannot separate psoriasis onset from psoriasis RECOGNITION, since a population with a psychiatric diagnosis is under greater medical surveillance than matched controls. The meta-analysis opposing it reaches the opposite conclusion for the same exposure class and finds that the pooled positive rests on retrospective recall of stressful events, on a time lag ranging from nine months to five years across studies, and on heterogeneity of 87 percent. Direction is unresolved in a second way the located anchors do not settle: psoriasis is itself highly stigmatising and psychologically burdensome, so a reverse route from psoriasis to a stress disorder is plausible and unexcluded. Individual claims require a dated PTSD diagnosis preceding documented psoriasis onset, recorded dermatological assessment establishing psoriasis independently of the psychiatric diagnosis, exclusion of prior psoriasis, of family history, and of smoking, alcohol, obesity and medication effects, and a surveillance-bias assessment.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Chronic traumatic stress engages the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal and sympathetic-adrenal axes with sustained catecholamine and glucocorticoid signalling, which in predisposed skin shifts keratinocyte behaviour and dermal immune trafficking toward the psoriasiform phenotype; the route the cohort's hazard ratio is consistent with and the route the stress-sensitivity reviews describe mechanistically, but whether the stress exposure produced any individual's psoriasis, rather than merely preceding its recognition in a more closely surveilled population, remains hypothesized until the psychiatric and dermatological timelines are read together.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at nationwide-population-based-cohort and systematic-review-meta-analysis class, and deliberately authored AS AN UNRESOLVED CONFLICT rather than as a supported edge: the registering cohort is placed first because it is the only located anchor measuring the exposure this catalog identity actually represents, a DOCUMENTED PTSD DIAGNOSIS, and the opposing meta-analysis is placed second and registered as the edge's COUNTERWEIGHT, not omitted, because it is the strongest available estimate and it concludes that no convincing evidence exists. The distinction between recalled stressful events and a documented stress disorder diagnosis is the hinge of the disagreement and is stated in the basis, the gaps and the alternatives, because the pooled positive of 3.4 rests entirely on the former at 87 percent heterogeneity while the only diagnosis-based estimate is 1.2 and null. BATCH 80 REFUSED THIS ROUTE ON THE META-ANALYTIC NULL AND THAT REFUSAL IS OVERRIDDEN HERE, recorded rather than applied silently, for one reason only: the registering cohort is diagnosis-based and post-dates the evidence batch 80 weighed in spirit but not in kind, so the conflict is now two-sided where batch 80 saw one strong null and a weaker counter-current. The override is limited to that reason and does not generalise to the alopecia or urticaria routes.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: THE LOCATED EVIDENCE DISAGREES AND THE EDGE IS REGISTERED FOR THE DISAGREEMENT: a nationwide cohort of 9,801 PTSD patients reports an adjusted hazard ratio for psoriasis of 3.81 (95 percent CI 1.90-7.67) while the systematic review and meta-analysis of 39 studies and 32,537 patients concludes that no convincing evidence exists and reports a null odds ratio of 1.2 (0.8-1.8) for the only study using a DOCUMENTED STRESS DISORDER DIAGNOSIS; no located design reconciles the two. SURVEILLANCE BIAS IS UNRESOLVED AND IS THE PRINCIPAL ALTERNATIVE READING: a population carrying a psychiatric diagnosis is observed more closely than matched controls, so incident psoriasis may be RECOGNISED more often rather than caused more often, and no located anchor adjusts for dermatological contact rates. The meta-analytic positive rests on recalled stressful events preceding onset, pooled from five studies under I-squared 87 PERCENT heterogeneity, with a time lag to recollection varying from nine months to five years, and recalled exposure is subject to recall bias in patients who already have the disease. Four of six studies of events preceding EXACERBATION, as distinct from onset, found rates comparable to controls. DIRECTION IS UNRESOLVED, since psoriasis is itself psychologically burdensome and a reverse route is unexcluded. The cohort is administrative-claims based and cannot control for smoking, alcohol, obesity or medication exposure.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Surveillance and detection bias: a population carrying a PTSD diagnosis has greater medical contact, so psoriasis may be recognised more often rather than caused more often
Reverse direction: psoriasis is stigmatising and psychologically burdensome, so a stress disorder may follow psoriasis rather than precede it
Shared upstream factors: smoking, alcohol, obesity, sleep disruption and medication exposure, none adjusted for in the registering cohort
Prior or subclinical psoriasis predating the PTSD diagnosis, and family history of psoriasis

heldEdges.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because the located evidence is genuinely two-sided for the first time on this route, a nationwide diagnosis-based cohort reporting an adjusted hazard ratio of 3.81 against a meta-analysis reporting no convincing evidence and a null of 1.2 for the same diagnosis-based exposure, and because the project's discipline is to register a contested claim at association only with the disagreement on its face rather than to let a prior refusal stand after the evidence changed shape. The edge states the cohort, states the counterweight, states the recall-versus-diagnosis hinge at 87 percent heterogeneity, and states surveillance bias as the principal alternative reading. Batch 80 refused this route on the null alone; that refusal is explicitly overridden here and the reason is recorded on the file so a later batch does not re-derive the conflict.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Stressful and traumatic exposures are associated with atopic dermatitis in systematic-review evidence, but the located material for this route is REVIEW-ONLY and NO EPIDEMIOLOGICAL COHORT WAS LOCATED that measures a documented post-traumatic stress disorder diagnosis against incident atopic dermatitis, so the edge is registered at association only with its anchor tier declared on its face: the PRISMA 2020 systematic review of 30 studies, restricted to low and moderate risk of bias and searched across Scopus, PubMed and PsycINFO from January 2000 to November 2025, reports stress- and trauma-related exposures associated with increased risk, earlier onset or greater severity of conditions including atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, alopecia areata and chronic urticaria, with associations strongest for early-life adversity and cumulative stress, and states explicitly that 'longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships' (PMID 42179055); the second anchor is a NARRATIVE review of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis function, neurogenic inflammation and immune dysregulation of skin under prolonged stress (PMID 41362509), registered for the mechanistic vector only and NOT for magnitude. The registered claim is therefore that stress and trauma exposures co-occur with and are reported alongside atopic dermatitis, with temporal order unestablished by the located evidence.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of atopic dermatitis is established for any individual: the only located positive is a systematic review which states on its own face that longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships, so the direction of the association is unestablished even in its own source; the second anchor is a narrative review rather than an epidemiological design and carries an AUTHOR-INDUSTRY CONFLICT OF INTEREST, its lead author declaring employment with and founder and chief scientific officer status at a skincare company; atopic dermatitis is itself intensely pruritic and sleep-disrupting, so a reverse route from the skin disease to a stress or anxiety state is a live alternative that no located anchor excludes; and no located anchor separates atopic dermatitis from the generic eczema identity, which this catalog holds separately and which owns the iatrogenic paradoxical-eczema route, so the atopic phenotype must be established on any individual claim rather than inferred from an eczema diagnosis. Individual claims require a dated stress or trauma exposure preceding documented atopic dermatitis onset, dermatological confirmation of the atopic phenotype, established chronology, and exclusion of contact dermatitis, of the iatrogenic paradoxical-eczema route owned by the sibling eczema identity, of allergen and irritant exposure, and of sleep disruption as a mediator rather than a consequence.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Sustained stress signalling through the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis and sympathetic outflow alters cutaneous barrier function and dermal immune set-point, lowering the threshold for atopic inflammation; the route the narrative review describes mechanistically and the route the systematic review's early-life-adversity gradient is consistent with, but whether the exposure produced any individual's atopic dermatitis or merely accompanies its severity remains hypothesized until pre-exposure and post-exposure dermatological findings are read against the stress timeline.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at systematic-review and narrative-review class, with AN ANCHOR-TIER DECLARATION as its principal limitation: NEITHER REGISTERED ANCHOR IS A COHORT, no epidemiological design was located measuring a PTSD diagnosis against incident atopic dermatitis, and the edge is therefore registered on a synthesis and on a mechanistic narrative rather than on any counted population. The systematic review is registered first because it is the only anchor naming atopic dermatitis specifically among its conditions and because it is restricted to low and moderate risk of bias; the narrative review is registered second FOR THE VECTOR ONLY and its industry conflict of interest is disclosed rather than suppressed. The review's own statement that longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships is carried in the basis and in the gaps so no reader takes the association as directional. A SCOPE GUARD is applied to the target: this identity is ATOPIC DERMATITIS specifically following the 2026-09-28 scope split, it is NOT generic eczema, and the sibling eczema identity owns the iatrogenic paradoxical-eczema route, so an eczema diagnosis does not satisfy this target and the two must not be conflated.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: AN ANCHOR-TIER DECLARATION THAT BOUNDS THE WHOLE EDGE: NEITHER REGISTERED ANCHOR IS AN EPIDEMIOLOGICAL COHORT. No located design measures a documented post-traumatic stress disorder diagnosis against incident atopic dermatitis, so this route has no counted population behind it and rests on one systematic review and one narrative review; the only diagnosis-based cohort located in this batch, the nationwide PTSD study, covers AUTOIMMUNE skin diseases and does not report atopic dermatitis, which is not an autoimmune classification. The primary anchor states on its own face that LONGITUDINAL STUDIES ARE NEEDED TO CLARIFY TEMPORAL RELATIONSHIPS, so direction is unestablished in its own source. The second anchor carries an AUTHOR-INDUSTRY CONFLICT OF INTEREST, its lead author declaring employment with and founder and chief scientific officer status at a skincare company, and is a narrative review at Cureus tier registered for mechanism only. DIRECTION IS UNRESOLVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: atopic dermatitis is intensely pruritic and sleep-disrupting and can itself generate distress. A SCOPE GUARD IS MANDATORY: the located literature does not consistently separate atopic dermatitis from generic eczema, while this catalog holds them as distinct identities after the 2026-09-28 scope split, so an individual claim must establish the ATOPIC phenotype and may not be satisfied by an eczema diagnosis or by a paradoxical drug-induced eczema owned by the sibling identity.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Reverse direction: atopic dermatitis is pruritic and sleep-disrupting and can itself produce a stress or anxiety state
The sibling eczema identity's iatrogenic paradoxical-eczema route, which a generic eczema diagnosis cannot distinguish from atopic dermatitis
Contact dermatitis and irritant or allergen exposure as independent causes of the same presentation
Sleep disruption as a mediator between distress and skin severity rather than as a consequence of either
Recall and attribution bias, since the primary synthesis relies substantially on self-reported exposure

nexusClaim.associationBasis: A documented post-traumatic stress disorder diagnosis is associated with incident alopecia areata in the nationwide population-based cohort that supplies the psoriasis route, and the smaller case-control evidence on which batch 80 withheld this route measures a DIFFERENT EXPOSURE and returns a PARTIAL NULL rather than a clean one, so the edge is registered at association only with the two exposures distinguished and the disagreement open: the Taiwan cohort of 9,801 PTSD patients and 39,204 matched controls reports an adjusted hazard ratio for alopecia areata of 4.77 (95 percent CI 2.47-9.20), the LARGEST of the individual autoimmune skin hazards in that analysis (PMID 33587564); against which the 2012 case-control study of 61 consecutive alopecia areata outpatients and 60 age- and sex-matched healthy controls found NO DIFFERENCE in the number or mean scores of PHYSICAL and SEXUAL stressful lifetime events between the groups, while patients reported a greater number and higher mean scores of EMOTIONAL stressing events, with higher scores on loss of a family member during childhood and on emotional neglect by relatives (PMID 23317485). The two are not directly contradictory, because one measures a DIAGNOSIS and the other measures RECALLED EVENT CLASSES, and the second's null is confined to physical and sexual events; but the second prevents this edge from reading as a general stress effect.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of alopecia areata is established for any individual: the registering cohort is administrative-claims based, cannot control for smoking, obesity, medication or healthcare-seeking intensity, and cannot separate alopecia areata onset from its RECOGNITION in a more closely surveilled psychiatric population; the case-control counterweight is SMALL, at 61 patients and 60 controls, is retrospective and recall-based, and returns a null for physical and sexual events while remaining positive for emotional events, so it supports at most an emotional-adversity reading and not a stress-general one; alopecia areata is visibly disfiguring and is itself a potent source of distress, so the reverse direction is a live alternative; and the located survey literature on this pair runs in the REVERSE direction and is deliberately NOT registered here. Individual claims require a dated PTSD diagnosis preceding documented alopecia areata onset, dermatological confirmation of patchy or total non-scarring loss, exclusion of prior alopecia and of family history, and exclusion of thyroid disease, iron deficiency, other autoimmune disease and traction or scarring causes.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Traumatic stress signalling is held to disturb the hair follicle's immune privilege through neuroendocrine and sympathetic pathways, permitting perifollicular lymphocytic attack on the anagen follicle; the route consistent with the cohort's hazard ratio and with the emotional-adversity signal in the smaller study, but whether the exposure produced any individual's alopecia areata or preceded its recognition remains hypothesized until pre-exposure and post-exposure dermatological findings are read against the stress timeline.

BATCH 80 WITHHELD THIS ROUTE ON THE CASE-CONTROL NULL AND THAT WITHHOLDING IS OVERRIDDEN HERE, recorded rather than applied silently: batch 80 read the second anchor as a null for the route, whereas on its own text the null is confined to physical and sexual events and the study is positive for emotional adversity, and batch 80 did not have the diagnosis-based cohort hazard ratio of 4.77. The override is limited to that reason. A DIRECTION GUARD is recorded against the reverse-direction survey literature, which is reserved rather than registered.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: THE TWO ANCHORS MEASURE DIFFERENT EXPOSURES AND THE EDGE CANNOT PULL THEM TOGETHER: the cohort measures a documented PTSD diagnosis against incident alopecia areata at an adjusted hazard ratio of 4.77 (95 percent CI 2.47-9.20), while the case-control study measures RECALLED EVENT CLASSES and returns NO DIFFERENCE for physical and sexual stressful lifetime events with positivity confined to emotional events, so the smaller study supports at most an emotional-adversity reading. THE COUNTERWEIGHT IS SMALL AND RECALL-BASED, 61 patients against 60 matched controls, and cannot support a precise estimate in either direction. SURVEILLANCE BIAS IS UNRESOLVED, the cohort being administrative-claims based with no adjustment for dermatological contact rates, smoking, obesity or medication, so recognition may differ from causation. DIRECTION IS UNRESOLVED AND THE REVERSE ROUTE IS STRONG: alopecia areata is visibly disfiguring and the located survey literature measures PTSD as an OUTCOME of hair loss rather than as its antecedent, reporting 33.9 percent of 1,449 respondents screening positive for PTSD relating to their hair loss experience and stating explicitly that a causal relationship cannot be deduced; that literature is RESERVED and NOT REGISTERED here, because using it forward would invert its own conclusion. No located anchor establishes whether the stress exposure precedes onset rather than severity or recurrence.

Emotional adversity specifically, rather than stress or trauma generally, as the operative exposure in the smaller study

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Stressful and traumatic exposures are associated with chronic urticaria in systematic-review evidence and perceived stress correlates with urticaria severity in a small physiological study, but NO LOCATED ANCHOR MEASURES A DOCUMENTED STRESS DISORDER DIAGNOSIS AGAINST INCIDENT URTICARIA and the one large cohort on this pair measures the REVERSE direction, so the edge is registered at association only with direction explicitly unresolved: the PRISMA 2020 systematic review of 30 studies restricted to low and moderate risk of bias reports stress- and trauma-related exposures associated with increased risk, earlier onset or greater severity of conditions including chronic urticaria, strongest for early-life adversity and cumulative stress, while stating that longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships (PMID 42179055); and the 2026 cross-sectional study of 100 examinees, 34 dermographic urticaria, 33 chronic spontaneous urticaria and 33 healthy controls, reports urticaria severity positively and linearly correlated with perceived stress (p = 0.004) and dermographism activity correlated with the Perceived Stress Scale (r = 0.347, p = 0.045) (PMID 41766900). The second is CROSS-SECTIONAL and establishes co-variation, not consequence.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of urticaria is established for any individual: the only primary study located is CROSS-SECTIONAL and measures perceived stress and urticaria severity at a single time point, so temporal order cannot be established from it and the correlation is equally consistent with urticaria generating distress as with distress generating urticaria; the systematic review states on its own face that longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships; urticaria is intensely pruritic, visible and unpredictable and is itself a recognised source of anxiety and sleep loss, so the reverse route is a strong alternative; and the single large cohort located on this pair, of 98,785 individuals per group matched on the US TriNetX network, MEASURES THE REVERSE ARROW, reporting incident psychiatric disorders AFTER chronic spontaneous urticaria diagnosis and a modestly increased risk of reaction to severe stress and adjustment disorders at a hazard ratio of 1.15 (95 percent CI 1.09-1.22), with no consistent increased risk for depression, schizophrenia or suicide-related outcomes; that cohort is RESERVED and NOT REGISTERED here, because it cannot support a stress-to-urticaria claim in either direction. Individual claims require a dated stress or trauma exposure preceding documented urticaria onset, dermatological confirmation of chronic versus inducible urticaria, established chronology, and exclusion of physical triggers, infection, thyroid autoimmunity, drug exposure and hereditary angioedema.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Stress signalling through the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal and sympathetic axes is held to lower the threshold for mast-cell degranulation and to amplify dermal neurogenic inflammation, so that wheal-and-flare activity rises with perceived stress; the route consistent with the observed severity-stress correlation and with the stress-sensitive dermatosis reviews, but whether the exposure produced any individual's urticaria or only its severity, and whether the arrow runs that way at all, remains hypothesized until pre-exposure and post-exposure dermatological findings are read against the stress timeline.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at systematic-review and small-cross-sectional class, with AN ANCHOR-TIER AND DIRECTION DECLARATION as its principal limitation: NEITHER ANCHOR MEASURES A DOCUMENTED STRESS DISORDER DIAGNOSIS AGAINST INCIDENT URTICARIA, the primary is a synthesis that names chronic urticaria among several conditions and asks for longitudinal clarification of temporal relationships, and the second is cross-sectional at 100 examinees and establishes co-variation only. THE ONE LARGE COHORT LOCATED ON THIS PAIR IS DELIBERATELY RESERVED AND NOT REGISTERED, because it measures the reverse arrow, incident psychiatric disorders after chronic spontaneous urticaria diagnosis at a hazard ratio of 1.15 for stress and adjustment disorders across 98,785 matched individuals per group, and registering it on a stress-to-urticaria edge would invert its own design and its own conclusion; it is named in the evidence gaps so the reviewer knows it exists and knows why it is excluded. A SCOPE GUARD is carried: the located material spans chronic spontaneous urticaria, chronic inducible urticaria and dermographic urticaria, while the catalog identity is the generic Urticaria label, so any individual claim must state which subtype is documented. This is the WEAKEST of the four stress-dermatology edges in this batch and is ranked last on that understanding.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: NO LOCATED ANCHOR MEASURES A DOCUMENTED STRESS DISORDER DIAGNOSIS AGAINST INCIDENT URTICARIA, which is the exposure this catalog identity represents; the registered evidence is one systematic review naming chronic urticaria among several conditions and one CROSS-SECTIONAL study of 100 examinees (34 dermographic urticaria, 33 chronic spontaneous urticaria, 33 healthy controls) that establishes co-variation of severity with perceived stress at p = 0.004 and of dermographism activity with the Perceived Stress Scale at r = 0.347, p = 0.045, and cannot establish temporal order. THE ONE LARGE COHORT ON THIS PAIR RUNS THE REVERSE DIRECTION AND IS RESERVED RATHER THAN REGISTERED: a matched TriNetX cohort of 98,785 individuals per group measures incident psychiatric disorders AFTER chronic spontaneous urticaria diagnosis and reports only a modest hazard ratio of 1.15 (95 percent CI 1.09-1.22) for reaction to severe stress and adjustment disorders, with NO consistent increased risk for depression, schizophrenia or suicide-related outcomes, and states that chronic spontaneous urticaria is not broadly associated with incident psychiatric disease; it therefore supports neither arrow of this edge and is named here so the exclusion is visible. DIRECTION IS UNRESOLVED AND THE REVERSE ROUTE IS STRONG: urticaria is pruritic, visible and unpredictable and is itself a source of anxiety and sleep loss. SCOPE IS UNSETTLED: the located material spans chronic spontaneous, chronic inducible and dermographic urticaria while the catalog identity is the generic label. PHYSICAL AND PHARMACOLOGICAL TRIGGERS are the commonest documented precipitants and are not stress-mediated.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Reverse direction: urticaria is pruritic, visible and unpredictable and is itself a source of anxiety and sleep loss
Physical triggers of urticaria, including pressure, cold, heat, dermographism, sunlight and exercise
Infection, thyroid autoimmunity including Hashimoto thyroiditis, and drug or NSAID exposure
Hereditary angioedema and other bradykinin-mediated oedema mislabelled as urticaria
Subtype confusion across chronic spontaneous, chronic inducible and dermographic urticaria

governanceNotes: D1 batch 89 (2026-09-28): four ASSOCIATION_ONLY draft-quarantined mappings added as ranks 20 to 23 pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md; mapping approval is not citation verification. THE BATCH NUMBER IS 89 AND NOT 81: batch 81 is already landed as PR #508 (bipolar-disorder to hypothyroidism). THIS BATCH IS REQUEST-DRIVEN, NOT BACKLOG-DRIVEN: it was asked for as stress-induced dermatological and autoimmune flare-up work, and no such catalog identity exists, so the work is expressed as four routes out of the PTSD identity, which is the catalog's documented stress disorder diagnosis and the exposure class the located evidence actually measures. ALL FOUR EDGES ARE REGISTERED FOR A DISAGREEMENT RATHER THAN FOR A SUPPORTING RESULT, and each carries its counter-evidence on its own face. Two anchors in this batch are shared across edges and are therefore ONE EVIDENCE SET AND NOT INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION: PMID 33587564 across the psoriasis and alopecia-areata edges, being the single nationwide PTSD cohort reporting both hazards, and PMID 42179055 across the atopic-dermatitis-eczema and urticaria edges, being the single systematic review naming both conditions. Eight reference uses over six PMIDs, all six confirmed absent from master-sources.json before authoring. THE CITATION-PURITY THRESHOLD CONSTRAINED THE REFERENCE COUNT: this file is draft:false with 27 verified reference uses, and scripts/validate-knowledge-base.js forces a mapping to draft: true when its unverified ratio exceeds 30 percent, so four three-reference edges would have reached 30.8 percent and would have UNPUBLISHED this identity and broken the published/draft pin. Each edge therefore carries exactly TWO references, its positive anchor and its counterweight, which holds the ratio at 8 of 35 and is also the sharpest form of the conflict each edge exists to record.

TWO RESERVED ANCHORS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT REGISTERED BECAUSE THEY RUN THE REVERSE DIRECTION, and both are named here so a later batch does not register them forward by mistake. PMID 37900780 is a 2023 US national survey of 1,449 respondents with alopecia areata reporting that 33.9 percent screened positively for PTSD specifically relating to their hair loss experience, with the highest PCL-5 scores in alopecia totalis and universalis, and its own conclusion states explicitly that a causal relationship between alopecia areata and PTSD CANNOT BE DEDUCED because baseline mental health was not assessed; it measures PTSD as an OUTCOME of hair loss and cannot support a ptsd-to-alopecia-areata claim. PMID 42403316 is a matched TriNetX cohort of 98,785 individuals per group measuring incident psychiatric disorders AFTER chronic spontaneous urticaria diagnosis, reporting only a modest hazard ratio of 1.15 (95 percent CI 1.09-1.22) for reaction to severe stress and adjustment disorders, NO consistent increased risk for depression, schizophrenia or suicide-related outcomes, and concluding that chronic spontaneous urticaria is not broadly associated with incident psychiatric disease; it measures the reverse arrow and is named on the urticaria edge's evidence gaps. Both are preserved as reserved literature per ME-29 and NEITHER is registered as a source entity or a reference use.

A REFERENCE-TO-PMID DISCLOSURE AND A SCOPE GUARD apply to the atopic-dermatitis-eczema edge. AN ANCHOR-TIER DECLARATION BOUNDS THAT EDGE: NEITHER OF ITS TWO ANCHORS IS AN EPIDEMIOLOGICAL COHORT. The only diagnosis-based cohort located in this batch, PMID 33587564, covers AUTOIMMUNE skin diseases and does not report atopic dermatitis, which is not an autoimmune classification, so it cannot be used there; the edge therefore rests on one systematic review naming atopic dermatitis among several conditions and one NARRATIVE review registered for the mechanistic vector only. THAT NARRATIVE REVIEW CARRIES AN AUTHOR-INDUSTRY CONFLICT OF INTEREST which is disclosed on the edge and on the reference: the lead author declares employment with, and founder and chief scientific officer status at, INSTYTUM AG, a skincare company. A SCOPE GUARD IS MANDATORY ON THAT TARGET: following the 2026-09-28 scope split, atopic-dermatitis-eczema is ATOPIC DERMATITIS specifically and is NOT generic eczema, and the sibling eczema identity owns the iatrogenic paradoxical-eczema route from biologic therapy for psoriasis, so an eczema diagnosis does not satisfy this target and an individual claim must establish the ATOPIC phenotype. A SCOPE GUARD APPLIES SIMILARLY TO THE URTICARIA EDGE, whose located material spans chronic spontaneous, chronic inducible and dermographic urticaria while the catalog identity is the generic Urticaria label, so the documented subtype must be stated on any individual claim.

THE AUTOIMMUNE HALF OF THE REQUEST IS ALREADY REGISTERED AND NO EDGE WAS ADDED FOR IT. The request named stress-triggered autoimmune disease exacerbation; the PTSD identity ALREADY carries five IMMUNE_MEDIATED routes to systemic-lupus-erythematosus (rank 11), rheumatoid-arthritis (12), inflammatory-bowel-disease (13), multiple-sclerosis (14) and thyroiditis (15). Registering further stress-to-autoimmune routes would restate relationships the graph already resolves through those five, so the autoimmune request is DISCHARGED BY EXISTING EDGES rather than by new authoring, and this note records that it was considered and why nothing was added. The four edges authored here are the DERMATOLOGICAL half only.
